x: The next six to finish were Epsom boys, followed by Dewberry and Strange Croydon (wise fellows !) went over the proper course, as did Chorley and Canard.

Dewberry thought it was a track race and set up a very fast pace. At any rate, it served the purpose of taking our team men away from the crowd, and quite possibly accounts for us placing the first six men home.
Webb and Dewberry were also near the leaders. Nearing the brook Footer moved up with Nuti and Bicknell of Thames Valley just in front of them.
Ernie Duffett had found the going a little hard and had retired. Dewberry was running very well and although some distance was picking up very quickly.

Our first man to arrive at this point was Carter, 9th, and Dewberry, looking very distressed, 11th, but where were our next men? Runners passed by until Fletcher came along, 30th, and Canard, 37th; Chorley and Coleman were still further behind, and as Mitcham and Reading's fourth man had already pas…
George's boys, Young and Tame; after these Dewberry, followed by another St.

The start was a good one in which Cohen (Ashcombe A.C.), Joe Flower and Dewberry showed to advantage, then over half a mile of parkland and encircling the Deer Enclosure with the runners in the following order: Cohen, Allum, Penny, Jack Flower, Frank Webb, Nuti (T.V.H.), Carter, Dewberry, Morrell, R…

Dewberry stomped by me next, and in his wake came Frank Webb. Then came our old friend and International runner, Bignall, of Highgate Harriers, with Ernie Duffett, a former holder of this Belgrave Championship, in close company.
Entering the gate to the reservoir Belton led this bunch by a dozen yards or so with Carter in eleventh position and Smith, Bignall, Dewberry and Duffett in the next dozen places.

Judging by the recent Surrey County running our team has a decidedly improved look about it. for of that team Carter, Smith and Dewberry are eligible together with Frank Webb, Joe Flower and Wally Bayliss, the last two having scored in last year's team who were placed second.

At the start, Dewberry, Warboys and Allum sprang into the lead and were joined by Jack Flower before reaching the "village"; Allum, however, soon moved into first position and maintained it the whole way, gradually but steadily increasing the lead.
Carter and Bill Webb were just behind these two. Then came Dewberry and a man who has been placed in handicaps every time except once this season.

From this relay to the end the Club were supreme, going further ahead at each stage; Dewberry, Joe and Jack Flower and Robertshaw, in the order, all running their course in fine style, Jack Flower doing third fastest time for us.

S.) all running strongly in a bunch; then came Duffett, Dewberry, O'Kell, Summerfield and Walker, also going well. The very bleak wind seemed to trouble quite a lot of the competitors, although they could not complain about the "going," which was really light.

Alec Robertshaw is to be congratulated upon finishing fourth and deservedly winning the sealed handicap. Dewberry, C. Penny and Taylor also ran well, particularly the last two named, who were attempting ten miles for the first time.
Carter had improved to 15th place, Mains had dropped back to the 20th (this was due to a slight recurrence of the trouble he had in our ten miles championship) and with Dewberry, F.
Dewberry was first off for us, and ninth back—no comments, please. Off went Frank Webb and pulled up a place—we were 1 min. 30 sec. behind the leaders.
